Changing the language is not a quiet spoof: the app really does load that language and renders in it from then on. Left off, the app still sees the real system language, which contradicts the SIM it is being shown.

The number and the ICCID are made up to fit the carrier, and they stay put once drawn: a SIM whose serial changes between two calls gives itself away. Picking a carrier also sets the cell tower MCC and MNC, so the two cannot contradict each other.\n\nThe operator fields are read inside the app itself rather than over a system call, so LSPosed has to have this module scoped to that app for them to apply. The number and the ICCID work either way.

Most apps never ask the system where they are - they ask Google Play Services, and all the system ever sees is Play Services asking. An app like that sees nothing new until Play Services is on the same profile.\n\nThat covers every app which gets its location that way, not only this one.

SIM properties and system language are hooked inside %s. Add this app to Vector/LSPosed scope and restart its process; System Framework scope alone only covers system-side location, cell and Wi-Fi hooks.
Make sure you have correctly set up this module
Not hooked into system_server \u2014 scope this module to System Framework in LSPosed and reboot
This app provides configurable location, cellular, Wi-Fi, SIM identity, and language information to selected apps through the Xposed framework.

Enable the module and include System Framework in its scope, then reboot the device. Create a profile, configure the required items, and assign it to an app. SIM identity and language changes also require the target app to be included in the module scope and restarted.

Use this app only on devices and applications you are authorized to test. Changes may not take effect until the related app is force stopped or the device is restarted. Compatibility can vary between Android versions, ROMs, and hook frameworks.
